Arthur adjusted his tie, sweating profusely as he clutched the cage containing Barnaby, a macaw with a vocabulary that exceeded his own. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a catastrophic error in judgment. He hadn’t realized that Barnaby had been listening to Arthur’s late-night calls with his mother, who happened to be the CEO’s sister and a notorious gossip.

"Good morning, Arthur!" chirped Barnaby, perched on the edge of Arthur’s desk. "Your mother says the merger is a sham and the CEO is wearing a toupee made of regret!"

The entire open-plan office froze. The CEO, a stern woman named Mrs. Higgins, dropped her coffee mug.

Arthur’s eyes widened. "Barnaby, hush!" he hissed, diving under the desk.

"Shush, shush!" Barnaby mimicked perfectly, then added, "Also, the Q3 earnings are fake! I saw the spreadsheet! It’s all made up! Just like your hairline!"

Arthur scrambled out from under the desk, grabbing the cage. "He’s joking! It’s a bit! A comedy routine!"

Mrs. Higgins narrowed her eyes. "Is it? Because last week, Barnaby told me that the 'confidential' project name was actually 'Project Pancake' and that the budget was being spent on waffle irons."

"It’s a metaphor!" Arthur squeaked.

Suddenly, the IT director walked by. Barnaby leaned out. "Hey, Dave! You still haven’t fixed the printer! It’s jammed with your excuses! Also, Arthur’s tie is ugly!"

Dave the IT director turned bright red. "That’s it! I’m calling security!"

"No, wait!" Arthur pleaded, trying to cover the cage with a newspaper. "He doesn’t understand context! He’s just a bird!"

"Neither do I!" shouted the receptionist. "He just told me that the company’s new slogan is 'We Try Our Best, But Mostly We Fail'!"

Arthur realized the situation was spiraling out of control. He needed to distract them. He looked around frantically, spotting a whiteboard marker. He grabbed it and began drawing a circle on the whiteboard.

"Look!" Arthur yelled. "A circle! Isn’t it pretty?"
